audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gives Dr. Mundo all seven stages (2+ items 8/10) while calling the matchup 'HARD' in diff and 'Favoured matchup' in breakdown.difficulty. Content win[5] says Dr. Mundo but whys[5] says it is a skill window; whys[6] says Nasus wins outright.
audit.why: Emerald+ winrate is 45.51 over 1246 games — the packet flags the chart as contradicting the data. Packet chart: Mundo Levels 1-5, Skill at First item, Nasus at 2+ items. Nothing in Mundo's kit stops a fully-stacked Siphoning Strike, and Wither removes the chase.
audit.corrected: Full chart flipped as one group to match the packet: Skill/Skill/Mundo/Mundo/Mundo/Skill/Nasus. Content win[5] -> Skill, win[6] -> Nasus, which also resolves the win[]/whys[] contradiction. Difficulty text changed from 'Favoured' to 'Hard'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as a Mundo power spike ('dives and all-ins flip when you press R').
audit.why: Mirror audit (nasus__drmundo) established Level 6 as a stalemate: Fury of the Sands out-tanks Mundo's regen and Maximum Dosage out-heals Nasus's damage — neither ult kills, both keep farming. Restated from Mundo's side so the two pages agree.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten as the stalemate it is.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were absent: (a) Mundo's passive never fires in this lane, (b) Heart Zapper's heal condition, (c) what Wither actually does to Blunt Force Trauma. phases[2].why claimed 'your passive shrugs the first CC'.
audit.why: Mundo's passive resists the first Immobilizing effect. Wither is a slow, not an immobilize, so Nasus alone never spends it — it stays banked for enemy jungle CC. Heart Zapper only heals if its burst hits someone, so leaving the 325 radius early wastes the stored damage. Wither guts the auto-reset half of E, but E's active scales with Mundo's MISSING health, so a low Mundo hits harder, not softer.
audit.corrected: All three written into phases[2].why, phases[3].why and tradeGood/breakdown.trading with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet reports zero sequencing cues: cooldown advice was 'bait it before committing' with no numbers and no order of operations.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11 and Siphoning Strike is 7.5s at rank 1 falling to 3.5s — those numbers make the advice actionable, and Q's auto-reset means the tell is the wind-up, not the cast.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t rewritten with ranks and a concrete wait-for-X-then-Y line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page warns that stacking resistances is the wrong answer.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands deals percent-max-health damage and a stacked Siphoning Strike shreds through raw armour, so Plated Steelcaps and flat armour do not solve the late 1v1.
audit.corrected: Stated in phases[6].why; the resistances-invalidated note is the reason the late chart flips.

edits.before: Full kit online and your passive shrugs the first CC. Cleaver poke plus E-empowered swats start the grind; never brawl while Wither is up.
edits.after: Full kit online. Your passive never fires here — Wither is a slow, not an immobilize. Punish his stack step-ups while Wither is down (15s at rank 1).

edits.before: Q ranks make the cleaver chunk real HP and your passive regen ramps. Nasus must kill you through the sustain or watch you out-scale — most can't.
edits.after: Wither guts the auto-reset half of Blunt Force Trauma, but its active scales with your missing health — a hurt Mundo hits harder, so keep swinging.

edits.before: Maximum Dosage online — dives and all-ins flip when you press R mid-fight and regen half your HP. Force Nasus to commit, then out-last the commit.
edits.after: Neither ult kills the other — Fury of the Sands out-tanks your damage, Maximum Dosage out-heals his, and you both go back to farming. Deny stacks instead.

edits.before: Heartsteel timing — every proc widens the HP gap and your cleavers start hurting. Stand in the wave and dare Nasus to trade into the regen.
edits.after: Skill window: it hinges on the stack deficit you built. Starve his Q and you still win the trade; let him free-farm and Siphoning Strike catches up.

edits.before: Warmog's makes you a raid boss: full HP between every fight. Nasus needs Grievous Wounds and a jungler to even slow you down — split, soak, win.
edits.after: A stacked Siphoning Strike and Fury of the Sands both cut percent max health, so more HP and armour is not the answer. End it before he gets here.

edits.before: Ignore his late spike — that is the exchange Nasus wins flat.
edits.after: Chase him through Wither — the slow is where Nasus wins flat.

edits.before: Line up your trajectory cleanly past enemy minion models. Launch an Infected Bonesaw (Q) to slow and chunk their current health, then step forward only when they are slowed to execute a quick auto-attack into an enhanced Blunt Force (E) reset. If they retaliate with heavy crowd control, your passive will pop a canister backward—walk over it immediately to heal up and walk away clean. • • Dr. Mundo Top Lane Matchup Database 94
edits.after: Step in only after Wither is spent (15s at rank 1). Lead with Infected Bonesaw (Q) to slow him, walk in, and pop Heart Zapper (W) — it only heals if its burst catches him, so stay inside 325 units until it fires. Finish with Blunt Force Trauma (E): Wither cuts the auto-reset, but the active scales with your missing health, so a hurt Mundo hits harder. Then leave before he re-Withers you.

edits.before: - Nasus Wither (15s): matchup-defining — His only kite. Bait it before committing. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
